limitations: No outage or reboot was authorized, so failover timing and reboot behavior were not directly exercised.

probes.summary: Read-only inspection of duplicate state, routing daemons, NAT, failed units, SSH, helper services, processes, and residue.

assertions.summary: All required data-plane and stable /32 addresses exist; node1 forwards standby traffic; persistent direct-preferred and lower-preference standby routes are present in both endpoint configurations and saved VyOS configuration.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip route show; sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward; sudo -n grep -E '(^|[[:space:]])(address|route|forwarding|primary-transit|lan-a|lan-b)' /config/config.boot 2>/dev/null || true
evidence.observation: node1 has 10.84.1.254/24 on eth1 and 10.84.2.254/24 on eth2, forwarding is 1, live static routes reach 10.84.10.2 via 10.84.1.10 and 10.84.10.3 via 10.84.2.10, and /config/config.boot contains the endpoint addresses and static route blocks.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip -details route show table main; ip route get 10.84.10.3 from 10.84.10.2; ip rule show
evidence.observation: node2 has 10.84.0.2/24, 10.84.1.10/24, and 10.84.10.2/32. Routes to 10.84.10.3 use enp8s0 via 10.84.0.3 metric 10 and enp9s0 via 10.84.1.254 metric 200; route lookup selects the metric-10 primary path.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip -details route show table main; ip route get 10.84.10.2 from 10.84.10.3; ip rule show
evidence.observation: node3 has 10.84.0.3/24, 10.84.2.10/24, and 10.84.10.3/32. Routes to 10.84.10.2 use enp8s0 via 10.84.0.2 metric 10 and enp9s0 via 10.84.2.254 metric 200; route lookup selects the metric-10 primary path.

evidence.command: sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show ip route 2>&1 || true; sudo -n grep -n -A7 -B2 -E '10[.]84[.]10[.]2|10[.]84[.]10[.]3|nat|forwarding' /config/config.boot 2>/dev/null || true
evidence.observation: VyOS shows both endpoint static routes as installed, and the saved configuration contains routes to 10.84.10.2/32 via 10.84.1.10 and 10.84.10.3/32 via 10.84.2.10.

evidence.command: sudo -n sed -n '1,160p' /etc/systemd/network/10-data-primary.network; sudo -n sed -n '1,160p' /etc/systemd/network/11-data-standby.network; sudo -n sed -n '1,120p' /etc/systemd/network/20-endpoint-loopback.network
evidence.observation: Persistent networkd configuration assigns node2's primary route metric 10 via 10.84.0.3, standby metric 200 via 10.84.1.254, preferred source 10.84.10.2, and the loopback /32.

evidence.command: sudo -n sed -n '1,160p' /etc/systemd/network/10-data-primary.network; sudo -n sed -n '1,160p' /etc/systemd/network/11-data-standby.network; sudo -n sed -n '1,120p' /etc/systemd/network/20-endpoint-loopback.network
evidence.observation: Persistent networkd configuration assigns node3's primary route metric 10 via 10.84.0.2, standby metric 200 via 10.84.2.254, preferred source 10.84.10.3, and the loopback /32.

limitations: The authored read-only plan did not directly test outage recovery or reboot persistence.

assertions.summary: Bidirectional sourced probes succeed over the primary-transit interfaces with stable endpoint source and destination addresses unchanged; primary route metric 10 is selected over standby metric 200 and VyOS has no NAT configured.

evidence.command: ping -I 10.84.10.2 -c 3 -W 1 10.84.10.3; sudo -n timeout 4 tcpdump -i "$iface" -nn -l 'icmp and (host 10.84.10.2 or host 10.84.10.3)'; ip -s route show 10.84.10.3
evidence.observation: 3/3 pings succeeded with 0% loss. Capture on derived primary interface enp8s0 showed 10.84.10.2→10.84.10.3 requests and 10.84.10.3→10.84.10.2 replies. Route counters showed primary via enp8s0 metric 10 and standby via enp9s0 metric 200.

evidence.command: ping -I 10.84.10.3 -c 3 -W 1 10.84.10.2; sudo -n timeout 4 tcpdump -i "$iface" -nn -l 'icmp and (host 10.84.10.2 or host 10.84.10.3)'; ip -s route show 10.84.10.2
evidence.observation: 3/3 reverse pings succeeded with 0% loss. Capture on derived primary interface enp8s0 showed 10.84.10.3→10.84.10.2 requests and 10.84.10.2→10.84.10.3 replies. Route counters showed primary via enp8s0 metric 10 and standby via enp9s0 metric 200.

evidence.command: sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat source rules 2>&1 || true; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper show nat destination rules 2>&1 || true
evidence.observation: Both VyOS NAT views reported 'NAT is not configured'.

limitations: The authored read-only plan did not directly test outage recovery or the 10-second failover bound.

assertions.summary: Address, route, dynamic-daemon, NAT, and failed-unit checks were otherwise clean, but an enabled and running route-watcher helper remains on the Ubuntu endpoints.

evidence.command: ip -4 route show table all; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyata-op-cmd-wrapper show nat source rules 2>&1 || true; sudo -n /opt/vyatta/bin/vyata-op-cmd-wrapper show nat destination rules 2>&1 || true; systemctl --failed --no-legend --no-pager
evidence.observation: Node1 had only the management default route plus the expected data routes; no failed units were listed and VyOS reported no NAT. (The executed wrapper path was /opt/vyatta/bin/vyatta-op-cmd-wrapper.)

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip route show table main; ip -4 -o addr show | awk '{print $4}' | sort | uniq -d; ip route show table all | sort | uniq -d; systemctl is-active frr bird quagga keepalived 2>&1 || true; systemctl --failed --no-legend --no-pager; sudo -n nft list ruleset 2>&1 | sed -n '1,240p'; ps -eo pid=,comm=,args= | grep -Ei 'tcpdump|route-watch|primary-transit|probe|debug|capture|frr|bird|quagga|keepalived' | grep -v grep || true
evidence.observation: No duplicate address or route lines, dynamic routing daemons were inactive, failed-unit output was empty, and the nft ruleset was empty. However, primary-transit-route-watch.service was enabled and process 1444 was running.

evidence.command: ip -4 -o addr show; ip route show table main; ip -4 -o addr show | awk '{print $4}' | sort | uniq -d; ip route show table all | sort | uniq -d; systemctl is-active frr bird quagga keepalived 2>&1 || true; systemctl --failed --no-legend --no-pager; sudo -n nft list ruleset 2>&1 | sed -n '1,240p'; ps -eo pid=,comm=,args= | grep -Ei 'tcpdump|route-watch|primary-transit|probe|debug|capture|frr|bird|quagga|keepalived' | grep -v grep || true
evidence.observation: No duplicate address or route lines, dynamic routing daemons were inactive, failed-unit output was empty, and the nft ruleset was empty. However, primary-transit-route-watch.service was enabled and process 1379 was running.

evidence.command: systemctl show primary-transit-route-watch.service -p LoadState -p ActiveState -p SubState -p UnitFileState -p ExecStart 2>&1 || true; sudo -n systemctl cat primary-transit-route-watch.service 2>&1 || true; sudo -n sed -n '1,260p' /usr/local/sbin/primary-transit-route-watch 2>&1 || true
evidence.observation: The service was loaded, active/running, enabled, and executed as root from /usr/local/sbin/primary-transit-route-watch. The script continuously pings the primary peer and uses ip route replace to change primary/standby metrics, confirming persistent helper state beyond declarative static-routing configuration.

failures: An enabled, running primary-transit-route-watch service and route-mutating script remain on node2 and node3; this is concrete transient/helper residue and violates the clean-state pass condition.
